name: Mount Madonna Center
aka: Mount Madonna Center for the Creative Arts and Sciences
tradition: Hindu/Yoga (Classical Ashtanga Yoga in the lineage of Baba Hari Dass)
about: Mount Madonna Center is a yoga and meditation retreat center and intentional community set on 380 acres of redwoods and meadows on a mountain summit overlooking Monterey Bay, founded in 1978 and inspired by the teachings of master yogi Baba Hari Dass. It offers classical Ashtanga Yoga (the eight-limbed path) rooted in the Yoga Sutras, Bhagavad Gita and other Vedic texts, alongside a College of Ayurveda and School of Yoga. Guests can join multi-day annual group retreats (spring, summer, winter/New Year's and a fall silent meditation retreat), self-guided personal overnight retreats, and a wide range of yoga and Ayurveda programs and workshops. Daily life includes pranayama, meditation, asana, kirtan, and optional devotional practice at the on-site Sankat Mochan Hanuman Temple. Three vegetarian meals a day are served in the community dining hall, and a Wellness Center offers Ayurvedic and massage therapies for an additional fee.
technique: Classical Ashtanga (eight-limbed) Yoga: pranayama, meditation, asana, and kirtan in the Baba Hari Dass lineage.
teacherAccess: Guided group retreats led by experienced teachers with talks and dialogue; personal retreats are self-directed with optional drop-in yoga/meditation classes.
retreatOptions: Self-guided personal stays (min 2 nights, extended stays available) and 4-5 night annual group and silent meditation retreats.
schedule: Optional daily rhythm of morning and afternoon yoga/meditation classes, temple arati, and communal vegetarian meals.
cost: Personal retreats roughly $93-$303 per person per night by lodging type (meals and facilities included); group retreat packages priced separately.

pricePerDay.notes: Per person per night for a self-guided Personal Retreat, including lodging, three vegetarian meals, and facilities use; $93 tent/vehicle site up to $303 private queen/yurt.

foodNotes: Three vegetarian meals daily (Sun-Fri; brunch and dinner on Saturdays), plus a tea bar and breads/spreads between meals.
workNotes: No work required of retreat guests; a separate rotational volunteer program exists for longer-term stays.
